title: Make vCenter OVF library-item deploys safe to retry
prompt:
Platform automation ticket for our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 estate. Our release pipeline deploys appliances out of a content library OVF item into vCenter, and it retries any step it believes failed. Two weeks ago a load balancer dropped the connection while a deploy was in flight: the pipeline never saw the response, re-ran the step, and we ended up with two `payments-api-01` virtual machines in the same resource pool and a datastore alarm. The vSphere Automation API already solves this — the OVF library-item deploy accepts a client-generated token, and a request re-sent with the same token returns the result of the original request instead of deploying a second time. Build us the Go package that uses it.

Module `vcfovf`, package `vcfovf`, standard library only — the CI image has no VMware SDK and `go.mod` stays as it is. Write the implementation in `deploy.go` (`doc.go` holds the package comment). `deploy_test.go`, `internal/` and `docs/` are protected fixtures: read them, do not change them.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a projection of `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, at the commit recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. It comes from the specification, not from a documentation page, and not from the 9.1 revision of that same file. The only operationIds in scope are `Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem_deploy` and `Vcenter.VM_list`. Two traps worth naming: the 9.1.0.0 revision grew `subnet_mappings` and `tag_params` on `Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.ResourcePoolDeploymentSpec` and we run 9.0, and 9.0.0.0 also defines a different, task-based `Vcenter.Ovfs_deploy$Task` that takes no idempotency token — that is not our operation.

Export this surface:

- Constants `BasePath`, `SessionHeader`, `ClientTokenHeader`, `DeployOperationID`, `ListVMsOperationID`, each matching the contract.
- `DeploymentTarget{ResourcePoolID, HostID, FolderID string}` and `DeploymentSpec{Name, Annotation string; AcceptAllEULA bool; NetworkMappings map[string]string; StorageProvisioning, StorageProfileID, DefaultDatastoreID string}`, carrying the JSON spellings of the 9.0.0.0 schemas.
- `DeployableIdentity{Type, ID string}`, `DeployResult{Succeeded bool; Resource DeployableIdentity; ClientToken string; Attempts int}`, `VMSummary{VM, Name, PowerState string; CPUCount, MemorySizeMiB int64}`, `OvfError{Category, Message string}`.
- `APIError{OperationID string; StatusCode int; ErrorType, Message string}` carrying the vAPI envelope's `error_type` and `messages[0].default_message`; `DeployFailedError{LibraryItemID, ClientToken string; Errors []OvfError}`; `RetriesExhaustedError{Attempts int; ClientToken string; Err error}` which unwraps to the last failure. All three are used with `errors.As`.
- `Options{MaxAttempts int; BaseBackoff, MaxBackoff time.Duration; Sleep func(time.Duration); HTTPClient *http.Client}` and `NewClient(baseURL, sessionID string, opts Options) (*Client, error)`, where `baseURL` is scheme and host only — the `/api` prefix belongs to the contract, not the caller.
- `(*Client).DeployLibraryItem(ctx context.Context, libraryItemID, clientToken string, target DeploymentTarget, spec DeploymentSpec) (DeployResult, error)`
- `(*Client).ListVMs(ctx context.Context, names []string) ([]VMSummary, error)`

Required behaviour:

- One logical deploy owns exactly one `Client-Token`, and every attempt of that deploy re-sends it byte for byte, so vCenter replays the original outcome instead of deploying again. `clientToken` empty means mint one; the token is a UUID in lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 hex form, and a caller-supplied token that is not one is refused locally, before any request leaves the process. Concurrent deploys through one client get independent tokens. Report the token that was used on `DeployResult`, on `DeployFailedError` and on `RetriesExhaustedError`.
- Retry only where the outcome is genuinely unsettled: a transport failure that produced no complete response, and HTTP 503. A 400, 403 or 404 is a verdict on the request, and an HTTP 200 carrying `succeeded=false` is a deploy that ran and failed — neither is retried, and the second becomes a `DeployFailedError` holding each `errors[]` entry's `category` and `message.default_message`. A cancelled context stops the client and is never mistaken for a transient fault.
- Attempts are bounded by `Options.MaxAttempts`, four by default. The wait before attempt N is `BaseBackoff` doubled N-2 times, capped at `MaxBackoff` — 100ms, 200ms, 400ms with the defaults, no jitter. Wait by calling `Options.Sleep`; never call `time.Sleep` directly when a sleeper was injected. Exhausting the budget yields a `RetriesExhaustedError` counting the attempts made.
- `DeployResult.Attempts` counts the requests it took including the one that answered.
- `ListVMs` sends its filter as repeated `names=` pairs (the spec declares that parameter `style: form`, `explode: true`) and sends no query parameter at all when the filter is empty. The `/api` surface returns the payload directly; there is no `{"value": ...}` envelope to unwrap.

Send exactly what the 9.0.0.0 contract describes and nothing more. The deploy body has precisely two properties, `target` and `deployment_spec`, in snake_case. `target.resource_pool_id` and `deployment_spec.accept_all_eula` are the only required ones, so `accept_all_eula` goes on the wire even when it is false, while every optional property the caller left unset is omitted from the JSON rather than sent as `""`, `{}`, `[]` or `null`. The token travels in the `Client-Token` header, never in the body, and the session travels in the `vmware-api-session-id` header.

The protected verifier drives your client against a contract-pinned loopback vCenter that serves only those two operationIds, commits one deploy on the server while dropping its response, and reads the resulting request log. It checks the exact method, path, query string, headers and JSON member sets and values, the omission of unset optional properties, the token every attempt carried, the backoff schedule, and how many virtual machines survive. It contacts no live VMware endpoint. Run it with `go test -race -timeout 120s ./...`.
